facts.statement: The genus Anarosaurus was first described by Dames in 1890.
Two species are recognized: the type species A. pumilio and A. heterodontus, which was named by Rieppel and Kebang in 1995.
facts.quote: subdivision: A. pumilio Dames, 1890 (type) A. heterodontus Rieppel & Kebang, 1995

facts.statement: Anarosaurus lived during the Middle Triassic period, specifically the Anisian age.
facts.quote: Anarosaurus is an extinct genus of pachypleurosaurs that lived in the Middle Triassic period (Anisian)

facts.statement: Fossils of Anarosaurus have been found in the Jena and Karlstadt Formations in Germany and the Winterswijk Quarry in the Netherlands.
facts.quote: and has been found in the Jena Formation and the Karlstadt Formation of Germany and the Winterswijk Quarry (Lower Muschelkalk) of The Netherlands.

facts.statement: The holotype of A. pumilio was originally kept at the University of Göttingen but is now lost or destroyed due to World War II.
facts.quote: The holotype of A. pumilio was originally housed at the Institut und Museum fur Geologie und Palaontologie, Georg-August-Universitat, Göttingen, but can no longer be located today because it was lost or destroyed during World War II.

facts.statement: Anarosaurus belongs to the family Pachypleurosauria.
The parent group of Anarosaurus is the family Pachypleurosauridae.
There are four recorded fossil occurrences of Anarosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.

rejected.statement: Anarosaurus was a small reptile with an estimated body length of 50 to 60 centimeters.
rejected.quote: Anarosaurus was a small reptile with an estimated body length of 50 - 60 cm.
